pilot.title: The opportunity I might miss
pilot.position: An example of the learning loop, not the agreed first chapter or week.
pilot.premise: Avery wants a weekend role helping a community venue. The employer cannot see evidence of teamwork in Avery's first response. The opportunity matters, but the character has a supported chance to revise.
pilot.focus: One job-ad requirement and one evidence-based response. This is not a complete application, full selection-criteria unit or summative assessment.
detailFocus: Identify the selected requirement in a job advertisement.
Use STAR (situation, task, action, result) for one response; SAO and CAR remain for later teaching.
Communicate relevant evidence to the intended employer.
pilot.choices: Choose between two fictional roles with the same learning demand, then choose a truthful example from school, home, volunteering or a supplied fictional case. Paid-work experience is not required.
pilot.safeStakes: The first response is returned for clarification. No real countdown, public failure ranking, permanent career lockout or loss of friendship/health points. Pause and retry remain possible.
pilot.fun: A role the player actually wants, a character who responds to their choices, visible improvement after a retry and a small optional original noticeboard joke. The appeal is agency and discovery, not a quiz with decorative travel.

beats.title: Something I want
beats.player: Choose a role and notice the opportunity it could open for Avery.
beats.teacher: Introduce the fictional setting and confirm the shared learning focus; offer a ready-made character.
beats.evidence: The chosen role and a short reason. Engagement information only.

beats.title: My first response is not enough
beats.player: Inspect the ad and try a short response. The employer asks: 'What did you actually do?'
beats.teacher: Observe what students notice before instruction. Do not grade the first attempt as a penalty.
beats.evidence: Save the first attempt and the requirement the student selected.

beats.title: Now I need the technique
beats.player: Compare a vague claim with a specific example; learn STAR and identify its four parts.
beats.teacher: Give explicit instruction, model one response and check understanding. Supply text and spoken alternatives.
beats.evidence: A brief practice response and feedback identifying the next improvement.

beats.title: Make a stronger case
beats.player: Write or dictate a new response, select relevant evidence and explain why it fits the requirement.
beats.teacher: Check relevance, the student's own contribution and the stated outcome. A sentence frame supports students who need it.
beats.evidence: Revised response, matched requirement and short explanation of the change.

beats.title: See what changed, then recover
beats.player: Receive a specific acknowledgement or a clear next revision. Revise without losing access to the opportunity.
beats.teacher: Review the response as meets / developing / needs support. Any future automatic checks assist, not replace, teacher judgement.
beats.evidence: Teacher review, feedback and any retry. Story acknowledgement is provisional, not an automatic cash award.

beats.title: Could I do this somewhere else?
beats.player: Match the approach to a different fictional ad and name one strategy worth keeping.
beats.teacher: Check transfer and ask whether the player cared about improving. Note confusion, friction and support needed.
beats.evidence: Exit response and a separate engagement observation. This does not establish whole-unit mastery.

proof.check: The response addresses the chosen requirement, identifies the student's action and gives a relevant outcome.
proof.method: Compare first and revised responses using a teacher-agreed rubric; include a different-ad exit check.
proof.threshold: Tania must set the pilot success threshold before classroom testing.

proof.check: The player can explain what they wanted, chooses to improve after feedback and notices a consequence.
proof.method: Observe voluntary revision, confusion and off-task friction; ask a short private reflection. Time on screen alone is not success.
proof.threshold: Agree observation criteria with Tania; no arbitrary retention target is claimed.

proof.check: The same learning can be completed without 3D navigation, paid-work history or timed pressure.
proof.method: Test keyboard, reduced motion, text alternative, pause/resume and absence/catch-up on target school devices.
proof.threshold: No learner is blocked from the required learning; unresolved access failures block release.

proof.check: Attempts, review and progress belong to the right student and class and survive resume.
proof.method: Test save/reload, identity, permissions, teacher review and repeat submissions with fictional accounts.
proof.threshold: No lost evidence, cross-student exposure or duplicate reward transaction in the agreed checks.

experiences.hook: Arrive in a town full of unrealised potential and choose a character that feels like yours.
experiences.stakes: Curiosity, identity and belonging; no penalty for skipping cosmetics.

experiences.name: The opportunity I might miss
experiences.hook: A job you want is advertised, but your first application does not show why you fit.
experiences.stakes: The character may miss this opportunity without recognising and addressing the requirements.
experiences.theory: Job-ad requirements, response methods, cover-letter purpose and format, SAO / STAR / CAR.
experiences.action: Inspect the ad, compare a weak and strong response, learn the structure, rehearse and submit a revised application.
experiences.evidence: Annotated ad, matched criteria, cover letter and a reasoned structured response. Teacher checks relevance, not just submission.
experiences.recovery: Specific feedback, another attempt and another suitable opening. No permanent career lockout.
experiences.payoff: Greater readiness and possible story opportunity; earnings and item amounts undecided.
experiences.setting: Employer notice / application service; physical building not fixed

experiences.stakes: A decision based on a misleading claim may cost time or narrow the character's options.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required
experiences.name: My plan no longer adds up
experiences.hook: Reduced shifts or an unexpected cost puts something the character cares about at risk.
experiences.stakes: A planned purchase or opportunity may be delayed unless the character adapts.
experiences.theory: Financial goals, tracking, budgeting, saving and investing, contingency and seeking assistance; life events and risk.
experiences.action: Inspect a fictional budget, seek instruction, compare options and revise the plan with a contingency.
experiences.evidence: Before/after budget, justified trade-off and support pathway. Fictional figures only; no personal family disclosure.
experiences.recovery: Support, alternative routes and another attempt remain available even at zero funds.
experiences.payoff: Preparedness and control over a revised plan; wealth is not the learning grade.

experiences.evidence: Proposal, budget and justification. Assess reasoning, not which project wins or who paid most tax.
experiences.recovery: Deferred proposals remain visible; absent students can contribute through an equivalent task.
experiences.payoff: A visible class-owned upgrade; interaction with town stage remains an open design decision.

experiences.recovery: Targeted feedback and another interview opportunity.
experiences.payoff: Greater capability and a possible role offer.

experiences.participation: Planned core experience; accessible equivalent required

experiences.action: Listen, clarify, process, analyse and form an improvement plan; practise applying a resilience model.
experiences.evidence: Response to feedback, an action plan and review of progress. Not a judgement of personality or mental health.
experiences.recovery: Coaching, adjusted goals and supported re-entry after setbacks.
experiences.payoff: Growth in capability and an informed next step.

experiences.evidence: A CPD plan and evidence of learning transfer and sharing. A training purchase alone is not mastery.
experiences.recovery: Affordable alternatives, help and revised timing after setbacks.
experiences.payoff: A wider range of possible futures and useful capability.

experiences.theory: Enterprise culture, culture types, successful characteristics and alignment with individual values.
experiences.action: Investigate workplace practices, compare evidence and explain a personally justified choice.
experiences.evidence: Culture comparison and a reasoned recommendation that considers alternatives and bias.
experiences.recovery: Plans can change; no single career, income or lifestyle earns a moral score.
experiences.payoff: Agency, self-knowledge and a chosen direction.

styleGuide.title: A believable world, with a sense of possibility
styleGuide.ethos: Career Empire should feel like a place a young person wants to step into: recognisable, welcoming and full of possibility. Its people have warmth and personality; its buildings have substance, purpose and life inside them. Contemporary architecture, rich planting, natural materials and carefully placed technology create an optimistic near-future town. The camera brings us close enough to care. Light invites us towards an opportunity; movement makes a discovery feel earned. The world can struggle, recover and flourish without losing its identity. The ambition is the depth, craft and emotional presence of the supplied ElevenLabs Town Hall films, translated into a coherent, playable 3D world.
styleGuide.translation: Rebuild the selected designs as spatially believable, walkable 3D environments. Do not simply place the existing isometric pictures on planes, rotate a flat facade, or keep white-background display platforms. A generated 3D-looking image or film is a visual reference, not a mesh, rig or finished playable asset.

principles.title: Modern by default; distinctive by purpose
principles.body: Use the approved ECC campus and pavilion family: warm limestone/pale brick, navy framing, timber fins, generous glass, verandas and layered native planting. Historic Town Hall art is retained comparison, not the everyday architecture target. Match material quality and human scale without duplicating every roof.

principles.title: Detailed and tactile, not photographically literal
principles.body: Use convincing stone, glass, cloth, timber, water and foliage with softened, deliberately designed forms. Keep contact shadows, consistent scale and readable silhouettes. Avoid low-detail clay placeholders as final art, shiny plastic surfaces, photographic people in a stylised town, and excessive micro-detail that disappears at play distance.

principles.title: Warm people, teen-appropriate presence
principles.body: Characters should convey curiosity, concern, confidence and recovery through expression and body language. Preserve identity from shot to shot and between studio and world. Translate the supplied pose-sheet warmth into natural 3D movement without making every character constantly smile or cheer. Do not silently replace the existing explorer's jacket with a blazer; approve wardrobe by character and context. Broaden representation through approved character designs, not random regeneration.

principles.title: Nature belongs to the town
principles.body: Use layered planting, varied grass, garden edges, water and places to pause. Integrate paths, ramps, crossings and bridges into continuous terrain. Retain the crafted richness of the selected 2D environment references, but remove their isolated tile presentation. A place should look explorable from ground level as well as understandable from above.

principles.title: Light reveals opportunity
principles.body: Use clear daylight for ordinary exploration and warm interiors against cooler exteriors for selected evening scenes. Maintain visible doors, faces and route surfaces. Cyan or teal marks useful technology and interaction; warm light suggests occupancy. Do not make every view dark blue, coat every edge in neon, or let bloom hide architecture. Night scenes are a lighting variant, not the universal palette.

principles.title: Three related visual layers
principles.body: The town is grounded and spacious. Learning tools and displays may use more focused technology effects. Rewards may briefly use stronger green, gold, cyan or violet celebration cues. Keep them recognisably related without putting a glowing reward-frame around the entire world. Colour is accompanied by symbols and readable text; the reward artwork does not determine game economics.

principles.title: The camera brings the player into the experience
principles.body: Use an aerial view to understand the town, then character-relative perspective to approach a place. Keep the destination readable, show a purposeful reaction where useful, and cross a believable threshold into a consistent interior. The supplied clips begin at ground level; the aerial-to-shoulder connection comes from earlier project guidance. Prefer steady movement over whip pans, excessive blur or unexplained cuts. Cinematics need a skip/reduced-motion alternative in the eventual game.

principles.title: Development changes care and activity, not identity
principles.body: Disrepair, Growth and Flourishing should retain the same underlying architecture, route graph and character proportions. Show weathering and reduced activity, then repair, then maintenance and life. A disruption is a separate temporary layer and personal progression is separate again. Do not turn disadvantage into ugliness or make a crisis erase all visual evidence of earned progress.

avoid: Flat isometric cut-outs presented as finished 3D conversion; single textured facades used for unrestricted orbit.
A uniform town of old-fashioned civic buildings, or an equally uniform town of glass boxes.
A constantly dark neon city, permanent portal spectacle, floating holograms without purpose or strong bloom over every edge.
Miniature white display islands, oversized toy proportions, blank interiors, floating feet and doors that cannot be approached.
Uncontrolled changes to faces, hair, uniforms, badges, building footprints, doorway locations or time of day between shots.
Baked-in generated text, invented school crests, copied cultural motifs, arbitrary reward values or new gameplay mechanics hidden inside an art brief.
workflow: Choose a named reference for each job: architecture, character identity, material/lighting and camera. Attach the actual files; filenames in a prompt alone do not give a generator access to them.
Write the asset's purpose and intended experience. Lock identity, silhouette, dimensions/scale, entrance position, materials, lighting and exclusions before requesting variations.

Reuse the approved source set first. Develop the dimensioned approach and modular kit in the separate candidate; additional reference generation or vendor spending requires explicit scope and approval.

Approve one reference set, then build or commission the actual mesh, materials, rig and animation. Reuse the same geometry for states and camera shots; do not generate a different building for every frame.

Compare a rendered film reference with a real-time engine test on target school hardware. Agree measurable asset, lighting and performance budgets before production; no frame-rate or film-quality promise is made by this guide.

Record source, prompt, tool/model/version where available, date, rights, parent references, output, approval status and runtime test evidence. Keep original references and editable source aligned with the live Blueprint record.

prompts.title: Core style block
prompts.text: Career Empire: semi-realistic ECC Career Campus + Campus-to-Career Corridor for a career-and-life simulation. Attach the current CE-CAMPUS-01, CE-CAMPUS-02 and relevant CE-STUDIO-CONCEPT-01 originals; these control architecture and material treatment. Warm limestone/pale brick, navy frames, timber fins, large glass, native planting and shaded walking paths. Restrained teal interaction; warm Western Australian daylight; believable human scale, entrance and ground contact. No toy-like blockouts, constant neon, copied civic monuments, invented logos or literal claims about ECC geography. Preserve selected character identity separately. A concept is not a mesh or finished playable scene. These templates do not authorise new generation or spending.

prompts.title: Selected building to 3D concept
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. SUBJECT: [named building and reference ID]. PURPOSE: [approved experience or reference study]. Reference A controls the selected building's recognisable silhouette, materials and activity; reference B, the approved campus/pavilion concept, controls the shared material and architectural quality. Older Town Hall frames are optional historical camera studies, not current building authority. Reinterpret this design as a complete walkable building at human scale. Keep [roof profile, material accents and distinctive features]. Show [ground-level three-quarter approach / side-rear view / one step inside the entrance] in [clear daylight / agreed evening light]. Keep the entrance usable and visible, integrate continuous ground and planting, and provide credible interior depth. Preserve the same building geometry across the set. [State] changes maintenance and activity, not footprint or doorway location. No detached display base, fake paper cut-out, copied Town Hall columns on every building, or conversion into a different architectural design. This output is concept reference only, not a production model.

prompts.title: Character to cinematic 3D reference
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. CHARACTER: [approved character ID]. Attach the identity reference and outfit reference separately. Preserve the approved face, hair, skin tone, approximate age, body proportions and identity-specific details. Match the warmth and expressive clarity of the supplied character poses while using dimensional facial forms, believable cloth, groomed stylised hair and grounded contact shadows. Keep the result appropriate for a Year 12 audience; do not silently de-age the character. Outfit: [approved outfit], with the exact badge placement and left/right accessories retained. Pose/action: [one natural action]. Camera: [full-body three-quarter reference / shoulder approach / expression close-up]. No face drift, random uniform redesign, mirrored badge/watch or permanently exaggerated grin. A reference image is not a rigged 3D character.

prompts.title: Building-entry video brief
prompts.text: Use the Core style block. Attach the approved character reference, building exterior, matching interior and, only for historical camera comparison, the selected Town Hall clip. No current campus film is supplied or approved by this template. Produce a proposed 8-10 second 16:9 reference film at the tool's supported output settings. Begin behind and slightly to one side of the character, looking towards the readable entrance. Move forward smoothly with grounded footsteps; let the destination fill more of the frame. Include a short, natural reaction only if it serves the moment. Cross the actual doorway into the matching interior without passing through a wall or changing the floor plan. Keep face, hair, outfit, badge, backpack, light direction and architecture consistent. ENTRY EFFECT: [restrained doorway light by default under existing guidance; use a stronger portal only after explicit approval]. If an effect is chosen, keep it local to the doorway and keep interior depth legible. No automatic aerial opening: request that as a separate connecting shot if needed. No teleport cut, sudden day/night swap, fisheye, camera shake, foot sliding, hard strobe, geometry morph, generated captions or invented interface. This is a visual reference; game timing and interaction remain separately designed.

prompts.title: Reward or tool graphic
prompts.text: Use the same Career Empire visual family but the focused interface/celebration layer. PURPOSE: [confirmed feedback state]. Create one clear [symbol or motif] with dimensional material, a restrained luminous edge and a clean silhouette. Use [approved role colour] against [transparent or specified background]. Preserve generous clear space for separately rendered text and values. No words, numbers, school logo or invented reward amount inside the generated image. Stronger glow is allowed locally for this brief celebration, not as the environment's permanent look. Keep the symbol readable without colour alone. Confirm the requested file format and transparency from the output, not from the prompt's promise.

checks: Could this asset and the supplied Town Hall film plausibly belong in the same world?
Does it preserve the selected design while adding credible depth, scale, material and movement?

Does technology support meaning, with stronger effects reserved for a purpose?
Can the eventual playable version meet access, camera, collision, rig and school-device requirements?
Are reference preference, proposed interpretation, accepted design and tested implementation labelled separately?

Completed changes need passed source/reader checks for every surface. Blocked or pending surfaces keep the change incomplete. Ready-for-publication is not complete: only publication may remain pending after every other required source/reader target passes. Completion requires the independent live check.
